title: Tight entropy contraction beyond detailed balance
abstract: We establish quantitative entropy contraction bounds for finite-dimensional quantum channels beyond detailed balance. For channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, we show that GNS (Gelfand--Naimark--Segal) norm contraction yields relative entropy contraction with only a logarithmic loss in the dimensional constant. For quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful asymptotic conditional expectation, this gives a lower bound on the complete modified logarithmic Sobolev constant in terms of the GNS spectral gap. The bounds allow initial entanglement with an external environment and are independent of its system size. Applications to alternating reservoir pulses and continuously coupled energy ladders give bounds with optimal size dependence.
summary: This paper develops new quantitative bounds for how quantum entropy contracts in open quantum systems, even when the system dynamics do not satisfy the detailed balance condition. By utilizing advanced tools from operator algebras, the authors establish relationships between relative entropy and spectral gaps for quantum channels. This is significant for understanding the fundamental rates of thermalization and relaxation in complex quantum matter models.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish quantitative entropy contraction bounds for general finite-dimensional quantum channels and quantum Markov semigroups, extending results beyond the restrictive condition of detailed balance.
main_result: It derives entropy contraction bounds that retain optimal logarithmic dependence on the system size, even when detailed balance is not assumed, providing lower bounds on the modified logarithmic Sobolev constant.
method: The analysis employs advanced tools from operator algebras, including GNS inner products, conditional expectations, and spectral gap analysis, to relate relative entropy contraction to spectral properties.
model_or_system: The study considers general finite-dimensional quantum channels ($\Phi$) and quantum Markov semigroups ($P_t$), applying the framework to specific physical models like energy ladders coupled to reservoirs.
key_observables: Relative entropy ($D(ho\|\sigma)$), GNS contraction coefficient ($s$), MLSI constants ($\alpha, \alpha_c$), and the spectral gap ($\lambda_{GNS}(L)$).
important_parameters: The bounds are shown to be independent of the external environment's system size, and the results are applicable to specific coupling strengths ($ eta$) and dimensions ($d$).
main_assumptions: The analysis requires the existence of a faithful conditional expectation ($E$) and a faithful invariant state ($\omega$), and is restricted to finite dimensions.
paper_structure: The paper develops the argument by first establishing GNS contraction coefficients for discrete time channels, then extending these bounds to the continuous-time quantum Markov semigroup framework, and finally applying the results to specific physical coupling scenarios.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, quantitative bounds on the rate of information dissipation (entropy contraction) in open quantum systems, which is fundamental for understanding thermalization and relaxation dynamics in complex quantum systems.
